{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"In Renaissance London, playing company was the usual term for a company of actors.","title":"Playing company"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" These companies were organized around a group of ten or so shareholders (or \"sharers\"), who performed in the plays but were also responsible for management.","title":"Playing company"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The sharers employed \"hired men\" that is, the minor actors and the workers behind the scenes.","title":"Playing company"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The major companies were based at specific theatres in London; the most successful of them, William Shakespeare's company the King's Men, had the open-air Globe Theatre for summer seasons and the enclosed Blackfriars Theatre in the winters.","title":"Playing company"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" The Admiral's Men occupied the Rose Theatre in the 1590s, and the Fortune Theatre in the early 17th century.","title":"Playing company"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Diederichs's stone (German: Diederichsstein, ) was a German monument in the city of Qingdao to commemorate Admiral Otto von Diederichs and the German occupation of the Kiautschou Bay concession on November 14, 1897.","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The monument was dedicated on November 21, 1898 by Prince Henry of Prussia.","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" It was located at an elevation of 98m, about halfway up the southwestern slope of the Signal Hill, the official German name of the mountain at the time was \"Diederichsberg\" ).","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Its most prominent feature was a plate decorated with the imperial eagle of the German Empire and the inscription \"For him who won for Kaiser and Reich the land all around, let this rock be named Diederichs's stone\" (\"Der hier für Kaiser warb u. [und] Reich ringsher das Land, nach ihm sei dieser Felsen Diederichsstein genannt\").","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" Below the plate was a rock inscription that read \"In this place on November 14th, 1897, Admiral v.[von] Diederichs took possession of the Kiautschou territory\" (\"Am 14.","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" November 1897 ergriff an dieser Stelle der Admiral v.[von] Diederichs Besitz vom Kiautschou Gebiet\").","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" A separate Chinese inscription was located to the right-hand side of the German text.","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":7,"text":" The entire monument stood about 5 meters tall.","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":8,"text":" After Japan occupied Qingdao in November 1914, a Japanese inscription (executed using Chinese characters: 大正三年十一月七日, \"November 7 of the third year of the Taishō period\") was placed across the imperial eagle.","title":"Diederichs's stone"},{"sentence_id":9,"text":" When Japan handed Qingdao back to the China on December 10, 1922, the monument was dismantled and parts taken to a military museum in Tokyo.","title":"Diederichs's stone"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"The Admiral's Men occupied which kind of theatre in the 1590s ?"}
